# Diagnose Pomegr reporting

Perform a read-only diagnosis. Do not edit files, emit or clear signals, invoke Pomegr tools as connection tests, or expose MCP configuration values.

## Policy

Resolve this plugin's `scripts/policy.mjs` relative to this file and run `node <script> validate --cwd <repository-root>`. Interpret its bounded JSON:

- `valid`: show path, byte size, Session progress state, and `delegatedAgents`. Version 6 is progress-disabled.
- `missing`: report repository-specific reporting as inactive and recommend `$pomegr:init`.
- `invalid`: show the bounded errors and recommend `$pomegr:init` to review an update.

## Automatic loading and delegation

For a valid policy, check for `[Pomegr reporting policy loaded]`. If absent, explain that the task may predate initialization or the hooks may not be trusted; direct the user to `/hooks` to review `SessionStart`, `SubagentStart`, and `SubagentStop`, then recommend starting or resuming a task.

Report delegation coverage. No rows means the main session owns reporting. Each declared type receives matching rows under `[Pomegr delegated reporting policy]` through `SubagentStart`.

## Optional usage guard

Report `.pomegr/usage-guard.json` as off when it is missing. If present, inspect only its bounded version-1 JSON fields: `version`, `mode`, `checkIntervalSeconds`, `warnAt`, `handoffAt`, `stopAt`, `concurrencyReservePercent`, and `maxConcurrencyReservePercent`. A valid active configuration has `version: 1`, `mode: "advisory"`, and `checkIntervalSeconds` of at least 60; `mode: "off"` is inactive. Report invalid JSON as inactive and recommend `$pomegr:init` to preview a repair. Handoffs follow the repository's existing workflow and conventions; no Pomegr handoff directory or ignore rule is required. Do not diagnose a missing handoff path or inspect handoff contents. It is an opt-in deterministic recommendation based on cached usage observations, never automatic enforcement, capacity confirmation, or a resume mechanism. Confirm the user trusts the optional `SessionStart` and `PostToolUse` hook definitions.

## MCP inventory

Check the resolved Pomegr namespace for `report_session_signal`, `clear_session_signal`, `report_agent_signal`, `clear_agent_signal`, `report_task_signal`, `report_session_progress`, `clear_session_progress`, `get_provider_health`, `get_usage_limits`, `list_sessions`, `list_session_agents`, `get_agent_context`, and `get_recent_failures`. Display only short names. Do not invoke them as a connection test. If any are missing, direct the user to the Codex plugin settings and `/mcp`. Do not read credential files or expose MCP configuration values. Read tools are decision-triggered observations; do not poll routinely or infer causation from coincident observations.

## Package structure

Verify `.mcp.json`, `hooks/hooks.json`, `scripts/policy.mjs`, the bundled progress reminder hook, and `scripts/usage-guard.bundle.mjs`. Also verify `skills/init/SKILL.md` and `skills/doctor/SKILL.md`. Confirm the hooks file registers `SessionStart`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, and an all-tool `PostToolUse` hook. This proves package structure, not runtime trust or execution.

## Role mappings

Run `node <repository-root>/monitor/agent-roles.mjs validate --cwd <repository-root>`. Report missing as inactive; otherwise show only bounded terminal diagnostics and accepted mapping keys. Explain that the monitor ignores an invalid file. Never expose mapping values or contents through browser-visible output.

## Result

Return a compact checklist for policy validity, automatic loading, delegation, optional usage guard, MCP tools, package structure, and role mappings. Include hook trust.

Never modify `AGENTS.md`, `.codex/config.toml`, `.codex/agents/*`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.pomegr/signals.md`, `.pomegr/usage-guard.json`, `.gitignore`, or application code.
